<RecipePage recipeId="skill-publishing-pipeline">

<RecipeSection label="Problem">

Teams can keep portable Agent Skills in source control, but they still need a repeatable way to validate the bundle Glean will accept, publish it under the caller's permissions, prove a later publish becomes a version rather than a duplicate, and inspect exactly what was stored. This recipe makes that lifecycle runnable without implying that the Skills API executes the skill.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeArchitecture />

<RecipePrereqs />

<RecipeSteps />

<RecipeSection label="Validate before persistence">

Call validate first and stop on any error. Validation itself never creates or updates a skill.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Confirm supersession">

If the validated display name already exists, show its ID and require confirmation before create adds a version.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Treat content as untrusted">

Stage downloaded bundles in a fresh bounded sandbox, never overwrite files, and never execute bundle contents.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Delete by captured ID only">

Deletion removes every version. Never choose a cleanup target by display name or a broad catalog search.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Experimental API">

The scaffold opts in with includeExperimental, but the Skills endpoints may still be unavailable on a tenant or change before general availability.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Publishing is not execution">

The API stores and distributes skill bundles. This recipe does not run the skill or prove how an agent host will interpret it.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="OAuth policy varies by tenant">

Native Skills scopes may not yet be grantable everywhere. The login wrapper uses the legacy compatibility scope only for a recognized scope-grant failure; a user-scoped token remains an explicit fallback.

</RecipeSection>

<TakeItFurther>

- Use glean.skills.createVersion() when your system already tracks a specific skill ID and explicit version creation is clearer than name-based supersession.
- Adapt the included GitHub Actions workflow so merges publish one stable skill name with a user-scoped secret and an explicit backend origin.
- Build a read-only catalog client that lists only the signed-in user's entitled skills and stages selected bundles for human review.

</TakeItFurther>
